chunks: And whoever performs seventy rakʿahs in Makkah,
and "Indeed, We sent it down," and the Verse of Subjugation, and Ayat al-Kursi,
he will not die except as a martyr.
And feeding in Makkah is like fasting elsewhere.
And fasting one day in Makkah equals fasting a year elsewhere.
And walking in Makkah is in the worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.آيَةِ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Ayat al-Kursi, a Qur'anic verse of great virtue
key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: Surat al-Qadr, recited here as part of the devotional act
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, the sacred sanctuary where acts of worship are greatly multiplied
key_terms.شَهِيدًا: a martyr, indicating an honored manner of death

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of prayer, fasting, and worship in Makkah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes special virtues connected to worship in Makkah, especially prayer with specific Qur'anic recitations, feeding others, fasting, and even walking there. It emphasizes the multiplied spiritual merit of acts performed in the sacred sanctuary and the elevated reward promised for them.
